<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-ownership-policies.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx`  _(via computeLayeredRlsFilter (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via computeLayeredRlsFilter (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class), registerAuthzMiddleware (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-ownership-policies.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **67** of **249** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 99fbaa6d1841e2556c48ba88de54226ae6b2de3f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fa6afb463398b2195cf811c9fff24838bb6db3aa` — the merge of head `4fe236dbd1652989eb591cd8ba2befce20e7261c` into base `99fbaa6d1841e2556c48ba88de54226ae6b2de3f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fa6afb463398b2195cf811c9fff24838bb6db3aa && git checkout fa6afb463398b2195cf811c9fff24838bb6db3aa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 99fbaa6d1841e2556c48ba88de54226ae6b2de3f 4fe236dbd1652989eb591cd8ba2befce20e7261c && git checkout -B drift-repro 99fbaa6d1841e2556c48ba88de54226ae6b2de3f && git merge --no-ff 4fe236dbd1652989eb591cd8ba2befce20e7261c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 99fbaa6d1841e2556c48ba88de54226ae6b2de3f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 99fbaa6d1841e2556c48ba88de54226ae6b2de3f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — REWORK (release text only) · head 2ba103da71349d3ac7f3bac97a6ad6fec8687375

The code, the vouch, the row scope, the pins, the ADR amendment and the docs all hold, as listed below. One item is owed: release text that ships in the same CHANGELOG as this note and that this PR makes false.

### To fix

1. **`.changeset/35802-predicate-write-floor-deferral.md` (the #35914 half, still unreleased in `.changeset/`) states the opposite of this PR in two places.**
   - The "What does not change" bullet reads "A `controlled_by_parent` detail keeps the floor on a predicate write, except on an update of a row that sits in a queue the caller belongs to … that half is not changed here."
   - Paragraph 4's clause reads "A row the service abstains on keeps the floor: … and on a `controlled_by_parent` detail unless an update's row sits in a queue the caller belongs to."
   - Both notes go into the same `@objectstack/plugin-security` CHANGELOG entry. A reader of that release would get one bullet saying the floor stays on this path and a second note saying it does not. That is release text this round makes false (checklist: "published defects this round made false"). It is not yet published, so correcting it costs a sentence rather than a second note.
   - The route exists. `os-dev.md` (editing an existing `.changeset/*.md`) and `landing-operations.md` (DELIBERATE CORRECTION) apply: no `skip-changeset`, `check-empty-changeset` stays red as it should, and the body declares DELIBERATE CORRECTION naming the note and quoting each sentence before and after.
   - Point both sentences at this PR's note. For example, the bullet could say a `controlled_by_parent` detail's predicate write is decided by its master gate (see that note), and the paragraph-4 clause could drop the `controlled_by_parent` arm.
   - Then the new changeset's sentence "whose bullet … no longer holds" can become a plain cross-reference. That one is yours to word.
   - The seat's confirmation of a release-text-only correction is an ACCEPT that quotes before and after. I will write it in my delta read, so the seat's Fable and four-piece step still runs once, on the final head.

The head changes, so declare the new final green head in a PR comment and message me. I will read the delta.

### Checked and holding

- **Shape:** `l1-face.mjs --pr 36282` at 2ba103da71 shows 42 success, 17 expected skip, 0 failed and mergeable_state clean.
  - The declarations are `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` · `Metadata-protocol: none`. The `!` title and the BREAKING banner are first in the changeset, and the ADR-0087 disposition is `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The level is patch, which follows Metadata-protocol `none`.
  - `Fixes #35802` is right: with #35914's sharing half merged, this delivers the ruled remainder (7073030861 「A 批量与逐条一致」).
  - The dogfood battery ran in full on this head (484 files passed, no failure), which clears the face's one flag.
- **The vouch fails closed both ways.**
  - `judgeControlledByParentWrite` writes the row list into a WeakMap keyed on `opCtx` only after every refusal of the predicate leg: the master walk, the null-master owner rule and the body-named master.
  - The middleware reads it straight after the caller's own pass, and only when `!delegatorSets && addressedPredicateWrite(...)`.
  - If the gate judged nothing, or the middleware does not see an addressed predicate write, the value is `null` and the floor stays. A delegated write never reads it, and keeps both floors.
- **Row scope:**
  - The write is scoped to `{ id: { $in: rowIds } }`, the ids whose master reference the gate read. Those rows come from the caller-context read-door `find` of the caller's predicate under the 10,000 cap, and the cap throws rather than truncating.
  - It is ANDed with the caller's `where` and with Layer 0 (the tenant wall) and Layer 1, which `masterGateCoversThisWrite` composes without the floor and with every authored policy intact.
  - This closes P3 by construction: no row is written under the handed-over floor without its master having been judged. Ablation 3 and the row-inserted-after-the-read case pin it.
  - An empty `rowIds` scopes to nothing, which is right.
  - Step 3.6's post-image check is composed on the same decision. The sharing relief is skipped on a vouched write because there is no floor left to replace. It is not pinned, as the body says, and is harmless either way.
- **Pins:**
  - There are 24 new cases on the real-engine rig. Each caller (master owner, edit-share member, Modify All, `writeRequiresMasterRead`, `ownerMayEdit`, null-master, delegated) is compared row for row with by-id writes on a second copy. The refused-whole cases, all-or-none (409) and the late-insert case are covered.
  - The `[#8757] §3 RESIDUAL` pin is flipped with its comment corrected.
  - The two write-shape suites now expect `all` for a member and keep `own` for the delegated agent. Before that update the full suite failed on exactly those 4 cases.
- **Surface deviation (area question): no amendment owed.**
  - The four files outside the claim only deliver the claimed change: one comment in `security-plugin-rls-filter.ts`, the one `rls.mdx` sentence this change makes false, and the two tests that pinned the superseded outcome.
  - None changes another consumer's behaviour, and none is named in the body.
- **Text:**
  - The ADR-0055 amendment is a dated status line, a pointer under the superseded 2026-11-14 sentence, and a closing section quoting the ruling verbatim. No older amendment is rewritten.
  - The three permissions pages say the new rule, sentence by sentence.
  - `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` is carried by `Skills-docs: follow-up #36285`.
- **Gates:** `check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt` were NOT MEASURED locally. All three are carried by green CI at this head, which I accept.
- **Landing:** this is governed (Tier H, `docs/adr/**`) and narrowing, so after my ACCEPT it goes to the seat for Fable and the four pieces. The area does not land it.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (delta) · head cdb290f78314feb5018be3cd1151a972bc3e93bb

I read the delta from 2ba103da71 alone, after REWORK 7074592987. It changes 2 `.changeset/` files, +3/−3, and no code. Everything else that record checked stands. The dogfood battery's reading at 2ba103da71 stands, because nothing it runs changed.

### The DELIBERATE CORRECTION, sentence by sentence

**Note corrected:** `.changeset/35802-predicate-write-floor-deferral.md`, the #35914 sharing half, which is unreleased.

1. **Paragraph 4.**
   - **Before:** "A row the service abstains on keeps the floor: on an object with no `owner_id`, on a delete under `public_read_write` (an update there has no floor to keep, because that OWD opens row updates), and on a `controlled_by_parent` detail unless an update's row sits in a queue the caller belongs to."
   - **After:** "A row the service abstains on keeps the floor: on an object with no `owner_id`, and on a delete under `public_read_write` (an update there has no floor to keep, because that OWD opens row updates)."
   - **Judgement: true at this head.** On a non-delegated addressed predicate write of a `controlled_by_parent` detail, step 3 now composes Layer 1 with `masterGateCoversThisWrite` and skips the sharing relief (`!predicateMasterGateRowIds`). So the abstain-or-queue path no longer decides that detail's rows. The two remaining arms are unchanged.
2. **The last "What does not change" bullet.**
   - **Before:** "A `controlled_by_parent` detail keeps the floor on a predicate write, except on an update of a row that sits in a queue the caller belongs to, … Its by-id write is decided by the master gate instead of the floor, and that half is not changed here."
   - **After:** "A `controlled_by_parent` detail is not decided by this composition. Its predicate write, like its by-id write, is decided by its master gate instead of the floor: see the note "a predicate update or delete of a `controlled_by_parent` detail now writes every row its caller may write by id"."
   - **Judgement: true at this head.** The quoted title is a verbatim prefix of the new note's first line. The delegated write, which keeps both floors, is stated by the bullet just above it, which is unchanged.
3. **This PR's own note.**
   - **Before:** "…shipped beside it (the note "…"), whose bullet "A `controlled_by_parent` detail keeps the floor on a predicate write" no longer holds."
   - **After:** "…shipped beside it: see the note "a predicate update or delete now writes the rows a Modify All holder, a non-creator owner or an edit-share target can write by id" for every other object."
   - **Judgement:** the quote is a verbatim prefix of the deferral note's first line. The two notes now agree, and each points at the other.

### Checks

- **`Check Changeset` is red,** in both runs, for `check-empty-changeset` alone. It refuses the base-present `.changeset/35802-predicate-write-floor-deferral.md`, which is the DELIBERATE CORRECTION it names. No `skip-changeset` is hung, as the rule says. The other changeset gates in the same job pass: the ADR-0087 registration, and the level axis at patch.
- **Everything else** is 40 success and 17 expected skip.
- **Who confirms the correction.** Under `landing-operations.md`, a correction inside a PR that also changes code is confirmed by the same-head, at-tier L2 PASS record, which judges each rewritten sentence. The seat ACCEPT confirms it only when the diff is release text or comments alone. This PR changes code, so the seat's Fable contract review at cdb290f783 must judge the three sentences above. My REWORK said this ACCEPT would be the confirmation, and that was wrong for this PR.
- **Landing:** this is governed (Tier H, `docs/adr/**`) and narrowing, so it goes to the seat for Fable and the four pieces. It enters the queue red, under SKILL.md's three conditions.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cdb290f78314feb5018be3cd1151a972bc3e93bb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-rls-filter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-ownership-policies.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/predicate-write-floor-deferral.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/controlled-by-parent-detail-write-authority.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/controlled-by-parent-every-master-edit.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/controlled-by-parent-write-shape-master-edit.test.ts
Security-touching: yes

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The diff.** 15 files, +575/−59, against merge base `a5a5312ff4`. Five source files and four test files in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src`, one ADR, three permissions docs, two changesets. No file under `packages/spec`, no `index.ts`, no `package.json`. The delta from `2ba103da71` (the head the dev report and the dogfood battery name) is the two changeset files, +3/−3, and nothing else.
2. **Where the vouch is taken.** `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:1668`–`1670`, inside step 2.8, on the line after the caller's own `assertControlledByParentWrite` returns. It is taken only when the write is not delegated and `addressedPredicateWrite` is true (not nested, not the referential clear, and the engine's own dispatch says `multi`).
3. **Where the record is written.** `security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts:694`, the last statement of the predicate leg of `judgeControlledByParentWrite`. Every refusal of that leg is above it: each master's chain walk, the owner rule for each null-master row, and the master the body names. The function returns at `:503` for an object that does not declare `controlled_by_parent`, and it takes this leg only when no single id is addressed and the engine's dispatch says `multi`. So a record exists only for a predicate write of a `controlled_by_parent` detail that the gate admitted.
4. **A stale record cannot be used.** The record is keyed by the operation object. The early returns of the gate depend on the object and the shape of the operation, not on the principal, so the caller's own admitted pass always rewrites the record before the middleware reads it. The delegator's later pass rewrites it too, but the middleware has read it by then, and only when the write is not delegated.
5. **What the vouch changes, three places.**
   - Step 3, `:2829`–`2835`: Layer 1 is composed with `masterGateCoversThisWrite`.
   - Step 3, `:2894`–`2896`: the row scope is `id IN (the gate's row list)` in place of the second read.
   - Step 3.6, `:2273`: a predicate update's per-row check is composed with the same option.
   - Two guards follow from it: the sharing relief is skipped (`:2915`) and the per-row floor-drop judge is skipped (`:2532`), because there is no floor left to replace.
6. **The floor comes off only on a detail.** `masterGateCoversThisWrite` is read in one predicate, `platformFloorYieldsToObjectWriteModel` (`security-plugin.ts:4535`–`4547`). It answers true only when the object declares `controlled_by_parent` and the operation is in the update or delete class. So even if the option were passed for another object it would drop nothing. Both guards hold independently: the record exists only for a detail, and the drop happens only for a detail.
7. **The row scope only narrows.** The gate's `rowIds` are the rows of its second read (`:1133`–`1148`), which is `id IN (the read door's answer for the caller's predicate)`. So the list is a subset of what `readableRowsScopeForPredicateWrite` returned before. An empty list composes `id IN ()`, the same shape the old scope composed for an empty answer.
8. **By-id parity, read in the code.** A by-id write of a detail passes `masterGateCoversThisWrite = !delegatorSets` at step 2.7 (`:1484`). The predicate path now passes the same option under the same exclusion, to the same `computeLayeredRlsFilter` and `computeWriteCheckFilter`. The app-authored policies and the write-visibility derivation are composed by that one function for both.
9. **No gate verdict moves.** The only change in the gate is the record and the extra member of `CbpPredicateWriteSelection`. That type is the return of a `private` method and the module is not re-exported from the package entry, so the published surface does not move.
10. **Checks at this head.** 59 check-runs: 40 success, 17 skipped, 2 failure. Both failures are `Check Changeset`, and in both the failing step is "Reject an empty-frontmatter changeset added by this PR". That is the DELIBERATE CORRECTION red. The PR is draft, with no auto-merge and no requested reviewer.
11. **Pins and ablations.** Not re-run (read-only review). The pins run on the file's real rig: `SecurityPlugin`, `ObjectQL`, the SQL driver on better-sqlite3, `SharingService`. Each case writes by predicate on one seeded copy and by id on a second, and asserts both the equality and the named set, so a case cannot pass by both sides being wrong in the same way. I counted, from the test source, the cases each ablation should turn red:
    - vouch set to null: 7 per verb in the new describe (14), the hook case, the late-row case, 2 in the flipped pin, 4 in the two write-shape suites (the member's selecting write on three legs in one file, and the member's case in the other): 22. The dev report says 22.
    - the new describe alone on unchanged `main`: 16. The dev report says 16.
    - per-row check left on the floor: 7 predicate updates, the late-row case, 1 in the flipped pin, and the same 4 write-shape cases, each of which runs a predicate update: 13. The dev report says 13.
    - second read in place of the gate's list: the late-row case, 1. The dev report says 1.
    - delegated exclusion removed: the two delegated cases, 2. The delegator in that pin holds Modify All, so only the agent's floor holds the rows back, and the pin does tell the two apart. The dev report says 2.
    The reported counts match the test design on every leg.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-security`, with `!` in the title, the BREAKING banner, both declaration lines and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) in the changeset body. That is the level AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 sets for a non-protocol breaking change. `Metadata-protocol: none` is true: no key, accepted value, metadata type, export or response member is added or removed. `Clause-②: no` is true: no published schema and no accept set moves. The `(narrowing)` arm is the one ruling item 5 orders.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Governed path.** `docs/adr/**` is in the diff, so the whole PR is Tier H and waits for the maintainer's approval. This record does not land it.
- **Ruling.** `Ruling-ref: 7073030861`. I read the comment. The PR body and the ADR quote the option label and its consequence line word for word. Items 1 to 6 are each built, and I found nothing built beyond them (see ④).
- **Dev deviation: four files beyond the claim.** Accepted. `security-plugin-rls-filter.ts` is a comment that said the bulk path "does not and must not" vouch. `rls.mdx` is a published sentence that said a predicate write on a detail keeps the floor. The two write-shape test files pinned the superseded outcome for a member's selecting write. Each is a statement this change makes false, and leaving any of them would have been the finding.
- **Dev deviation: P3 closed in the PR, not reported as a fork.** Accepted. The ruling names the route: "the dev either reuses one id list or shows…". The PR reuses one id list.
- **Dev flag: the skip of the sharing relief is not pinned.** Accepted as a nit (N3). With the floor absent from Layer 1 the relief has no floor to replace.
- **Open questions.** None raised.
- **Out-of-scope findings in the dev report.** The skill text is carried by #36285, which exists, is open and is in the skills lane. The contradicting changeset bullet was corrected in the delta. Both answered.
- **DELIBERATE CORRECTION.** One unreleased note is corrected, `.changeset/35802-predicate-write-floor-deferral.md`, and this PR also changes code, so this record is the confirmation. The three sentences are judged in ④. All three are correct at this head.
- **SQL push-down.** No new id materialisation and no in-app join. The gate's id list dates from #25012 and the `id IN` scope from #21829. This PR reuses the first in place of the second and removes one read.
- **Author.** The PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- **Security-touching.** `yes`. Every source hunk changes when the platform ownership floor applies to a write.

### ④ Design judgment

**Does the code make predicate writes match by-id writes on a detail, and only that?** Yes.
